sections.html: Sillaginopsis panijus can reach approx. 40 cm total length and is subject of an important commercial fishery. It belongs to the family Sillaginidae, which contains only 30 species. There is no accepted common name for this family; FishBase suggests "smelt-whitings". Suggestion for a common name: Longfin surferfish.

The difference between "foodfish" and "ornamental fish" is often hard to tell. For example, who in Europe would term the zebra barb (Danio rerio) a foodfish? Nevertheless hundreds of thousands of these tiny animals are collected daily in India, dried and sold as a spice. On the other hand, young examples of attractive foodfish can be found quite regularly in the ornamental fish trade, because fingerlings are easily available in large numbers due to the aquaculture of these species. Sillaginopsis panijus is an example of the latter category.

Available size: 5-6 cm.
In the wild the fish inhabits muddy regions and is anything but demanding. Only juveniles live in pure freshwater; larger fish and adults should be kept in brackish or marine water.

Sillaginopsis panijus is a very attractive aquarium inhabitant, for it is a restless swimmer of a somewhat sharky appearance, and the always erect dorsal spine is a real eye-catcher. The species is peaceful and omnivorous and should be kept in schools (5 or more specimens).
The presumed males can be recognized even at a much smaller length (around 5 cm) by the much longer head and dorsal filament.
Sexual maturity is reached at about 12 cm total length.

Sillaginopsis panijus is still an absolute rarity in home aquaria, and it will be an interesting experience to discover the life history of the species under aquarium conditions.

Lexicon: Sillaginopsis means about "similar to a small Sillago"; Sillago is another genus of the family Sillaginidae. panijus: after the Bengal name of the fish.
